hero.oneLiner: Secunderabad-based manufacturer and trader of adhesive tapes, die-cuts, polishing compounds, buffing pads and car care products for the automotive OEM and auto refinish markets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Secunderabad-based manufacturer and trader of adhesive tapes, die-cuts, polishing compounds, buffing pads and car care products for the automotive OEM and auto refinish markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sumax Engineering Limited manufactures adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes, domes and graphics and car care products, and additionally trades electrical and pneumatic tools, abrasive sheets/discs/rolls, body shop consumables, retail products and accessories and aerosol products. Products are sold into the automotive OEM paint shop and the auto refinish / body-shop aftermarket, with further application in consumer durables (domed labels for refrigerators, air conditioners, microwaves) and general industrial and hardware use. Manufacturing runs from two units, at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu) and IMT Manesar (Haryana), under ISO and IATF certified processes.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Autokrom India Private Limited — Group Company: CIN U34101TG2012PTC079468, incorporated February 29, 2012; identified as the sole Group Company by Board resolution dated March 09, 2026 on the basis of related party transactions in the last three years; registered office at Plot No.45, Shantiniketan Colony, the same address as the Company's registered office. Both Mr. Sudeep Mehta and Mrs. Smriti Mehta hold directorships in it.
- Mrs. Vimla Mehta — Selling Shareholder: Offering up to 1,00,000 equity shares in the Offer for Sale; consent letter dated March 26, 2026
- Lodha Corporation Limited — Other Indian directorship of Whole-Time Director Mrs. Smriti Mehta: Disclosed under her other directorships in Our Management
- Lagnam Spintex Limited, MMP Industries Limited, Usha Martin Limited — Other Indian directorships of Independent Director Mr. Vijay S Bapna: Disclosed under his other directorships in Our Management

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Manufacturing:** Adhesive Tapes and Die-cuts (automotive and industrial masking tape, PVC fine line, decorative masking, acrylic foam, aluminium, duct, surface protection and filament tape; small die-cuts and large-area masking), Pre-Taped Masking Film, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds, Buffing Pads and Foam Pads, Reflective Tapes, Domes and Graphics (domed labels and domed emblems), Car Care Products
- **Trading:** Tools - Electrical and Pneumatic (orbital sanders, rotary/orbital/angle polishers, dust extraction units, hand blocks), Abrasive Sheets, Discs & Rolls, Body Shop Consumables (masking paper, masking film OPS, compounding wool pads, foam pads, light weight body filler, backup pads, tack cloth), Retail Products and Accessories, Aerosol Products (silencer coat, brake parts cleaner, carb & choke cleaner, chain cleaner, chain lube and lubrication spray, rust penetrant)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Automotive OEM paint shop - paint protection, dual-tone masking and bumper masking die-cuts
- Auto refinish / body shop aftermarket - detailing, refinishing and surface preparation
- Consumer durables and white goods - domed labels and emblems for refrigerators, air conditioners and microwaves
- Industrial, hardware and packaging applications
- Domestic India - 99.36% of revenue for the period ended September 30, 2025; 99.47% in FY25
- Exports - 0.64% of revenue for the period ended September 30, 2025; 0.53% in FY25

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes itself as operating both a manufacturing division (adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes, domes and graphics, car care products) and a trading division (tools, abrasives, body shop consumables, retail products, accessories and aerosols), so a portion of what it sells is bought-in rather than made. On the inbound side it is not backward integrated: raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro are sourced from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers, with imports from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, the United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey; the cost of raw material consumed represented 37.01%, 43.26%, 44.29% and 47.10% of total revenues in the period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively. Conversion is done in-house at two manufacturing units (Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu and IMT Manesar, Haryana) using UV machines, dome machines, filling machines, label printing machines, shrink tunnels, pre-tape masking paper machines, masker roller machines, die-punching machines and cone high-lift pallet trucks, with an in-house testing laboratory and an R&D team; the Company states it is among the few with in-line doming application units. Outbound, the Company states it operates a Kanban / Just-in-Time inventory system to minimise stock levels, and reaches market through a dual-segment route: direct long-term B2B supply to automotive OEMs, and distributors, e-commerce platforms and direct sales for the B2C/B2B refinish market.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Raw material cost as a share of total revenues has fallen steadily - 47.10% in FY23, 44.29% in FY24, 43.26% in FY25 and 37.01% in the period ended September 30, 2025
- EBITDA margin expanded from 6.32% in FY23 to 8.84% in FY24, 10.21% in FY25 and 11.80% for the period ended September 30, 2025 (margin computed on Total Income)
- PAT margin, on revenue from operations, rose from 3.66% in FY23 to 5.69% in FY24, 6.84% in FY25 and 8.08% in the period ended September 30, 2025
- Revenue growth has been uneven - 35.18% in FY23, 3.13% in FY24 and 11.72% in FY25
- Mix is anchored on Adhesive Tapes and Die-cuts (48.13% of revenue in FY25, 45.00% in the period ended September 30, 2025), with Abrasive Sheets, Discs & Rolls the largest traded line (19.94% in FY25, rising to 24.12% in the period ended September 30, 2025)
- Business is almost entirely domestic - exports were 0.53% of revenue in FY25 and 0.64% in the period ended September 30, 2025
- Balance sheet is lightly levered - debt-equity ratio of 0.15 in FY23, 0.17 in FY24, 0.16 in FY25 and 0.13 as at September 30, 2025
- Return ratios improved through the track record - RoNW 14.75% / 19.11% / 20.42% and RoCE 19.70% / 23.32% / 24.63% for FY23 / FY24 / FY25; the September 30, 2025 figures of 10.60% and 12.89% are half-year and not annualised
- Inputs such as jumbo rolls, solvents, skins, heat film and velcro are sourced from a mix of domestic and foreign suppliers, so input cost is exposed to global commodity cycles, duty changes and currency movement

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Add manufacturing capacity through two new units - RIICO Karoli, Tapukara (Rajasthan) and Model Economic Township, Jhajjar (Haryana) - funded from the Fresh Issue proceeds
- Deepen the North India manufacturing footprint, with both proposed units in the NCR/Rajasthan belt alongside the existing Manesar unit
- Fund incremental working capital requirements to support the scale-up
- Deliver innovative and high-performance solutions through an all-inclusive portfolio catering to the evolving demands of both automotive manufacturers and the aftermarket industry
- Use the NSE EMERGE listing to enhance visibility and brand image among existing and potential customers and to create a public market for the equity shares in India
- Continue R&D-led development of highly reliable, robust and versatile products, with the team constantly observing market needs and trends

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company proposes to construct two new manufacturing units out of the Fresh Issue proceeds: proposed Unit I at Plot No E-185, RIICO Industrial Area, Karoli, Tehsil Tapukara, Rajasthan, and proposed Unit II at Plot No. P 32, Street No. B, Sector 11, Model Economic Township, Village Nimana, Tehsil Badli, District Jhajjar, Haryana. Both are greenfield builds that would add to the two existing units at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu) and IMT Manesar (Haryana), concentrating incremental capacity in the North India automotive belt close to the Manesar OEM cluster. The remaining objects of the Fresh Issue are funding of working capital requirements and general corporate purposes. In the text available the rupee amount for each object is the issuer placeholder, and no added capacity or commissioning date is printed against either proposed unit.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Experienced management team - stated by the Company as a qualitative factor for the offer price
- Long standing relationships with customers - stated qualitative factor
- Consistent financial performance - stated qualitative factor
- Promoter continuity: Mr. Sudeep Mehta has been integral to the Company since incorporation in 1994 and brings over 30 years of Automotive OEM experience
- Among the few companies with in-line doming application units, enabling high-quality acrylic domed labels for plastic, wood, metal and glass surfaces
- Full quality certification stack for automotive OEM supply - ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018
- Combined manufacturing and trading portfolio spanning both the OEM paint shop and the auto refinish aftermarket
- In-house R&D team plus robust infrastructure with latest precision tools and a well-equipped testing laboratory
- Batch-level quality control - adhesion peel, heat resistance through automotive baking cycles, residue-free removal, tensile strength and elongation, and paint-system compatibility testing
- Customisation offered to meet the diverse requirements of clients

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material price volatility and import dependence — Jumbo rolls, solvents, skins, heat film and velcro are global commodities imported from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, USA, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey; raw material cost was 37.01%, 43.26%, 44.29% and 47.10% of total revenues in H1FY26, FY25, FY24 and FY23. Duty changes and price cycles can compress margins where increases cannot be passed through.
- Product concentration in Adhesive Tapes and Die-cuts — A single category contributed 48.13% of revenue in FY25 and 45.00% in the period ended September 30, 2025; a change in OEM masking specification or a substitute technology would hit the largest revenue pool directly.
- Dependence on the automotive OEM and auto refinish cycle — Almost the entire portfolio is tied to vehicle paint shops, body shops and detailing demand, so a downturn in automotive production or refinish volumes flows straight through to revenue.
- Geographic concentration in the domestic market — Exports were 0.53% of revenue in FY25 and 0.64% in the period ended September 30, 2025, leaving effectively no external market to cushion an India demand slowdown.
- Promoter and key-man dependence — Mr. Sudeep Mehta, associated since incorporation in 1994, leads the entire management team and oversees overall management, day-to-day affairs and strategic decision-making.
- Execution risk on the two proposed greenfield units — Both proposed units - RIICO Karoli (Rajasthan) and Model Economic Township, Jhajjar (Haryana) - are to be constructed from Fresh Issue proceeds, and the text available prints no commissioning timeline or added capacity against either.
- Manufacturing concentrated in two locations — All current output comes from Unit I at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur and Unit II at IMT Manesar, with no alternate in-house capacity disclosed to absorb a disruption at either site.
- Foreign exchange and cross-border trade exposure — The Company flags import and export regulations that may erode profit margins or restrict trade, changes in foreign exchange controls and tax rates, and fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates including devaluations, alongside shifts in regional and local economic conditions.
